page: Amazon Web Services a1.4xlarge is an ARM64-based server powered by the first-generation AWS Graviton processor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.3 GHz using the Cortex-A72 ARMv8 architecture, with no hyperthreading. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates moderate multi-core performance with notable single-core and memory bandwidth tradeoffs. The server achieves average results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as average performance in Redis SET operations and Passmark database operations. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is weak to poor, and single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests, rank in the lower percentiles, reflecting the limitations of the first-generation Graviton core design.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the a1.4xlarge offers a low-cost entry point into ARM-based architecture, trading off raw single-core speed and memory bandwidth for dedicated physical core density. It is suitable for scale-out workloads that benefit from physical core isolation without requiring high memory-per-core ratios, such as basic web serving, containerized microservices, and development environments targeting ARM64 targets.

This server offers qualitative cost efficiency for ARM64 development and scale-out workloads that prioritize physical core density over high memory-per-core ratios, making it suitable for containerized microservices and basic web serving.
